recipes.name: Chef John's Shepherd's Pie
ingredients_raw: 1.25 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cubed

steps.text: Place cubed potatoes and garlic in a large pot with enough water to cover; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes.

Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Meanwhile, cook ground beef in a skillet over medium heat. Stir flour into beef and drippings; stir in vegetables, beef broth, ketchup, salt, and black pepper until combined. Cook until thick, about 5 minutes, then transfer to an oven-proof casserole dish.
Drain potatoes and garlic; return them to the pot. Slightly smash potatoes and garlic with a potato masher; add sour cream and 1/4 cup Cheddar cheese. Mash until smooth.
Top beef mixture with potatoes, spreading from center of casserole to edges to form top layer. Sprinkle with remaining 1/4 cup Cheddar cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until cheese melts and turns golden, 20 to 25 minutes. Cool before serving, 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Shepherd's Pie
raw_recipe.description: This easy shepherd's pie is made with lean ground beef and veggies, topped with creamy garlic mashed potatoes for a comforting weeknight casserole.

review.reviewBody: This was a great recipe (as are all of Chef John's)! I made a few additions and took some tips from other reviewers. First, I wanted it to be a more traditional Shepherd's Pie, so I used ground Lamb instead of beef. I diced 1/4 cup onion and 1/2 cup mushrooms and cooked it in with the Lamb as I was browning it. After the meet was finished, I added in a pinch of Thyme, Paprika, and a dash of Worcestershire sauce. I then continued with the original recipe. The last thing I did, after the dish was finished baking, I placed it under the broiler for a few minutes to make the cheese on top get nice and crispy.

I did not have any frozen vegetables in my freezer--I improvized. I threw in some chopped onion, chopped fresh zucchini, chopped fresh red pepper, and chopped fresh broccoli to take the place of the frozen vegetables. I also added a teaspoon each of dried oregano and dried basil to the meat/vegetable mixture and I cut back just a touch on the salt. I was able to use my cast iron skillet from beginning to end which I absolutely loved. My husband and two boys really liked this though my kids thought that it could use more cheese and my husband thought it could use more "gravy". Next time, I'll increase both the cheese amounts and "gravy" just a touch. This is absolutely comfort food defined.

Very easy to make, and tasted great. The potatoes were very creamy and flavorful, even with no butter added. The recipe didn't say when to add the salt and pepper, so I added it to the meat mixture. I also salted the water that I boiled the potatoes in. I wasn't sure what size casserole dish to use, but my 2-quart oval casserole worked perfectly. This is a great recipe for a quick, inexpensive meal. I'd like to try it using ground lamb also.

Its a keeper! Its a perfect way of using up leftover mashed potatoes, so that makes it even easier to make. I skip the sour cream since my leftover mashed potatoes already have butter and milk in them. I've made this twice now, both times with frozen veggies which works great. I follow the Recipe except I sauteed chopped onion and garlic with the meat, and add about twice as much broth to make more "gravy". I also add a few shakes of Worcestershire and maybe a little soy sauce to add a zip. Everything fits into a 2 quart casserole dish perfectly. Thanks Chef John!

First time making Shepherds Pie and it was a hit. I added about 6 cloves of garlic and 1/4 onion to the meat mixture and used veggie broth instead. I forgot the ketcup which made no difference. After smashig the potatoes I added garlic powder and pepper. The potatoes were so delightful that I make them as a side dish now. There are never any leftovers! 
Thanks John!!

Yes, I know you think that I should only give five stars if I tried and loved the recipe as written. And it's probably fine, as written. But it is such a fabulous basic recipe that I appreciate it, and rate it high. We like very savory food, so I added chopped onions, garlic, mushrooms and 1/2 tsp dried thyme to the ground beef as it cooked. A splash of wine with the beef broth; skipped the ketchup. For the topping, to make things easier, I used pre-made mashed potatoes, heated them up a bit and stirred in some cheddar and sour cream. Yum! Will make this again, using the same or different modifications.

Made this for my teen boys and stepdad tonight. All of them loved it. I threw some chopped jalapeños at the beginning when browning the meat. Also seasoned the meat with salt, pepper, onion powder (I didn't have an onion tonight), garlic powder, and minced garlic. I let some of the grease cook off and added in the flour and a bit of minced garlic. Let that cook for a couple minutes to ensure no floury taste. Added in the beef stock, maybe a teaspoon or so of better than bullion (roasted beef), the ketchup, and a few dashes of Worcestershire sauce. Then added frozen peas and carrots. Wish I'd added drained, canned veggies instead of frozen but that's what I get for not reading reviews first! I prepared Idahoan garlic potatoes and added butter, heavy cream, salt, and pepper. No sour cream. Topped the meat mixture with that. Topped potatoes with dried parsley and pepper. Didn't use cheese because stepdad and one teen dislike cheese. Those two rated it a 10/10. The cheese lover gave it a 9/10 and said only cheese could make it a 10. He is definitely my child lol

I loved it! 2nd time I used my mushroom stock & a bit of Marsala as well as a pinch of cayenne and 1/4 tsp dab of fenugreek powder; also used sriracha ketchup in the meat as well as sautéed an onion and my own canned mushrooms before I added just frozen peas. I put a small layer of drained canned corn on the meat mixture before spooning on the potatoes mashed with garlic & cheese & sour cream. I used a mix of 1/2 Parmesan cheese & 1/2 sharp cheddar-both freshly shredded/grated. It’s an awesome dish and can modify to my taste and what’s on hand. Great dish!
This Shepherds pie was good but the meat was a bit bland. I added a whole diced onion but next time I would add some garlic and a pinch of cloves to give it more flavour.

Delicious! Made exactly to the recipe. This is going into our meal rotation.I think onions and/or mushrooms would be great too. One tip for those (like me) who don't have a scale to weigh the potatoes... the ratio is 1:1 for the potatoes and the veggies. That's 4 cups each. I also cut down on the pans used by using my cast iron Dutch oven for browning the meat, mixing the veggies, and then baking in the oven.
Best Shepherd's Pie EVER!!! Made it twice now...just as delicious the 2nd time. I double the recipe, put it in 4 loaf pans so I can freeze 3 for a later date...and just as yummy!!

This is the best Shepherd's pierecipe I have made. I made it two weeks ago for our daughter (after surgery), SIL and our 4 Grand Littles. It was a hit, although the kids wanted to know where the pie crust was! haha! I'm making it tonight for the hubby and I and splitting it with my SIL and MIL. ❤️
Pretty good according to my husband... It's not quite like the one my mother use to make. Did a little of my own tweaking a bit; a couple more cloves of garlic and a dash of half and half.

Easy to make and delicious! Never leftovers when I make this recipe. For a fast week night meal, I used instant loaded mashed potatoes & it came out excellent! I have made it with homemade mashed potatoes too.
Great recipe just add some basic items or dice it up with extra ingredients. I found i didn't have enough potatoes. Next time I will add 2 small-med sized potatoes to the ingredients list.
I put too much sour cream but otherwise it was awesome.
My family loved it and the lamb was wonderful. I had lamb in the freezer and had no idea what to do with it. I'll be buying more lamb and making this wonderful pie!
Made it. The only constructive feedback was from my daughter who wished there was a little texture/crust on the top.
It was ok. Not the best Chef John's I ever had though. The rest of the family enjoyed it enough to eat their portion
Love it 😍
